In Support of LD 1453: Resolve, to Establish the innovative Factory-made Housing Working Group
April 25, 2025
Chair Curry, Chair Gere, and members of the Housing and Economic Development Committee;
On behalf of the Maine Real Estate and Development Association, please accept the following testimony in support of LD 1453: Resolve, to Establish the innovative Factory-made Housing Working Group. MEREDA's members consist of a wide range of people and organizations involved in real estate development in Maine, from architects and contractors to bankers and attorneys to developers and municipalities. Our members work together to support responsible development in
Maine.
MEREDA supports an all-hands-on-deck approach to meeting the state's housing needs, and
manufactured housing has a place in the solutions. The quality and diversity of manufactured
housing improved greatly since the mobile home park models of the 1970s. As noted by an article posted by the Urban Institute, "Manufactured homes cost significantly less than site-built housing, and the quality and appeal of manufactured homes built to US Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) standards has improved drastically." The fact that some of these homes are
manufactured right here in Maine is a bonus to our economy.
LD 1453 proposes a working group to further review how manufactured homes can be part of the
solution here in Maine. We support this bill because it is focused on finding solutions, similar to LD
1375, which is also looking at other barriers to housing construction and development. While we won't purport to tell you how you should structure these two committees should both bills be passed through the legislature, we highly recommend that they be closely intertwined to maximize
their potential. We encourage you to support this bill.
Thank you for your consideration of this testimony.
Elizabeth Frazier
On behalf of Maine Real Estate & Development Association

Testimony of Erik C. Jorgensen Senior Director of Government Relations & Communications Maine State Housing Authority
Before The Joint Standing Committee on Housing and Economic Development (132nd)
In support of LD 1453: Resolve, to Establish the Innovative Factory-made Housing Working
Group
Senator Curry, Representative Gere, and members of the Joint Standing Committee on Housing and Economic Development, I am Erik Jorgensen Senior Director of Government Relations and Communications at the Maine State Housing Authority (MaineHousing) and I am submitting this testimony in support of LD 1453: Resolve, to Establish the Innovative Factory-made Housing Working Group.
MaineHousing has been helping Maine people own, rent, repair, and heat their homes since 1969. We are an independent state authority (not a state agency) created to address the problems of unsafe, unsuitable, overcrowded, and unaffordable housing. We are authorized to issue bonds to finance single family mortgages for first time homebuyers and for affordable multi-family housing.
We are also authorized to administer a number of state and federal programs, including rental subsidies, weatherization, fuel assistance, two housing block grants,
1

the low-income housing tax credit program, and homeless grant programs. We receive state general fund revenue for homeless programs and receive a dedicated portion of the real estate transfer tax for the Housing Opportunities for Maine (HOME) Fund.
LD 1453 is a resolve proposing that a working group be established to study the potential of innovative factory-made housing technologies to reduce costs and accelerate production of housing in Maine. MaineHousing is enthusiastic about such a study group. As an agency we have seen increasing use of factory manufacturing techniques for projects in our production pipeline. We welcome this and agree with the sponsors that a better understanding of this type of technology would be very helpful for both affordable housing production, and more broadly understanding and supporting the factory-built housing industry in Maine.
Our experience has shown that units constructed in factories can be deployed in a fraction of the time needed for equivalently sized site-built projects, at lo loss of quality. We also feel that there is a potential for significant cost savings with those techniques, though that has yet to be fully realized.
The LD 1453 working group could provide a far firmer understanding of the industrial and economic factors that come together in producing factory-assisted housing. While the current working group structure of 36 members might prove unwieldy, we do have confidence in Senator Bennett's plan to refine the membership if this proposal moves forward.
Regardless of how this task force is comprised, MaineHousing would be honored to participate in it. We are especially glad to see that this proposal is for a task force that will sit outside of our agency, as the particular research duties enumerated in
2

section 5 extend well beyond MaineHousing's purview and expertise. These duties are appropriately broad and will draw from resources across state government as well as private industry. We feel this resolve has the potential to create significant new knowledge and generate a new State strategy concerning this type of housing technology. Creating housing in factories is a concept that occupies an important place in Maine's industrial history, and this bill has the potential to ensure that this history carries full-strength into the future. We are grateful to Senator Bennett for bringing this bill forward.

Testimony of Phoenix McLaughlin
Regarding LD 1453
Resolve, to Establish the Innovative Factory-made Housing Working Group
Senator Curry, Representative Gere, and members of the Committee on Housing and Economic
Development, my name is Phoenix McLaughlin, and I am the Director of Strategy Implementation at the Department of Economic and Community Development. I am here today to testify on LD 1453.
The question of how Maine can improve the way we build homes is a vital one for addressing
our strategic economic goals. This has been a growing area of interest for our department and others as it has the potential to address multiple economic needs at once: housing growth, workforce training, business development, and research and innovation. I, along with colleagues
from other agencies, have been researching what the State may be able to do to help improve
residential construction technology and methods, talking to industry experts and learning what
other states are doing.
Our work could benefit from the formal engagement of the Legislature. There is a range of
potential outcomes of this research, some of which may require legislation to implement. Having an element of legislative engagement through the summer and fall of this year could put us in a
better place to act on recommendations at the start of the next session. Our department would prefer to see changes to the text of the resolve to create a more manageable process, but the idea could dovetail well with our ongoing work.
Thank you for your time, and I am happy to answer any questions.

Friday, April 25
Senator Curry, Representative Gere, and honorable colleagues of the Joint Standing
Committee on Housing and Economic Development: I am Senator Rick Bennett of Oxford, and I have the honor of serving 14 communities in Western Maine in the State Senate. I am proud to sponsor LD 1453, "Resolve, to Establish the Innovative Factory-made Housing
Working Group."
LD 1453 is the result of a recommendation from HR&A Advisor's report, A Roadmap for the
Future of Housing Production in Maine. Among the many recommendations offered was
the creation of a group to look at innovative housing technologies.
In drafting this bill, there were many aspects and industries I had to consider but I wanted to keep the group small enough so it could still be effective. Even when I turned in the final draft to the Revisor's Office, I knew a lot of effort still had to be put in to get the working
group right. I am actively working with the Governor's Office of Policy Innovation and the
Future to further narrow both the group's membership and scope and want to thank the Maine Affordable Housing Coalition for all the help they have provided so far.
As we know from serving on this committee, it is essential that we examine ways to both lower the cost of housing and boost its production. This working group will examine some of the new technologies being used in Maine and around the country to meet the needed demand of 84,000 new homes by 2030.
Thank you for your time and patience. I hope to have a draft amendment soon that we can use at the work session. I would be happy to answer any questions.
